name: Rust
typeSystem: Static, strong, inferred, with affine types. Ownership and borrowing let the compiler enforce memory and thread safety in safe Rust without a garbage collector; unsafe code can opt out of some checks.

typeSystemExample.caption: Generic max with a trait bound on PartialOrd

runtime: Usually compiled ahead-of-time via LLVM to native code, with no language VM or garbage collector. Programs may link the standard library's allocation, threading, and other platform support, or use no_std.

runtimes.name: Native (rustc + LLVM)
runtimes.role: Default backend: highly optimised machine code with zero-cost abstractions and no GC.

runtimes.name: Native (rustc + Cranelift)
runtimes.role: Alternative backend focused on fast debug-build compile times rather than peak runtime speed.

runtimes.name: WebAssembly (wasm32 targets)
runtimes.role: First-class WASM support for browsers, edge runtimes, and plugins.

runtimes.name: Miri
runtimes.role: Interpreter for Rust's mid-level IR that detects undefined behaviour in unsafe code.

compilers.name: rustc
compilers.role: The official Rust compiler; uses LLVM by default.

compilers.name: rustc + Cranelift
compilers.role: Experimental nightly codegen backend aimed at faster debug builds.

compilers.name: gccrs
compilers.role: A Rust frontend for GCC, in development, widening platform reach.

compilers.name: mrustc
compilers.role: Independent compiler used mainly to bootstrap rustc from source.

asyncRuntimes.name: Tokio
asyncRuntimes.role: Multi-threaded, work-stealing executor. The de-facto standard for server-side async Rust (HTTP, gRPC, databases).

asyncRuntimes.name: async-std
asyncRuntimes.role: Mirrors the std API but async; multi-threaded executor with a familiar feel.

asyncRuntimes.name: smol
asyncRuntimes.role: Minimal, lightweight async runtime with a small API surface. Easy to embed.

asyncRuntimes.name: Embassy
asyncRuntimes.role: No-std async executor for embedded and bare-metal systems (ARM Cortex-M, RISC-V).

asyncRuntimes.name: Glommio
asyncRuntimes.role: Thread-per-core executor using io_uring for high-throughput, low-latency I/O.

asyncRuntimes.name: Compio
asyncRuntimes.role: Completion-based async I/O (io_uring on Linux, IOCP on Windows, kqueue on macOS).

asyncRuntimes.name: Monoio
asyncRuntimes.role: Thread-per-core io_uring-based executor from ByteDance, optimised for network services.

concurrencyModel: "Fearless concurrency": ownership and the Send/Sync traits prevent data races in safe Rust at compile time. OS threads are available via std::thread, plus async/await with pluggable executors (Tokio, smol, Embassy, etc.).

concurrencyExample.caption: 4 workers computing i*i in parallel via std::thread
